replies:
Here's the first question for a financial analyst interview:

"Tell me about yourself and why you want this role."

Answer out loud or paste your reply here (one to three minutes). I'll score it on structure, evidence and specificity, give one concrete improvement, then ask the next question. Ready?

Score: 2/10.

Why: Structure is weak (1) — it's just an action, not a STAR story. Evidence missing (0) — no measurable result or impact. Specificity low (1) — no tools, timeframe, company or your role named.
Rewrite (STAR, 2–3 sentences):
"At [Company], the finance team needed a credible forecast after revenue fell 8% year-over-year (Situation). I built a three-statement model in [your skill] that started from product-level revenue drivers, incorporated churn and pricing scenarios, and stress-tested assumptions against three public comps (Action). That model narrowed the planning range from a 10%–30% variance to a 5%–8% variance and led leadership to prioritize a 4% price increase, improving projected operating cash flow within one quarter (Result)."
One concrete improvement for your next shot: replace the placeholders with a real company name, the exact revenue decline you saw, the tool(s) you used ([your skill], Power BI, etc.), and a measurable outcome (dollar amount, percent change, months saved, or a decision that followed).

Next question: "Describe a time you found an error in a financial model — what happened and what did you do?"

Honest score: 2/10.

Why (brief):
- Structure (1/4): Your reply is an action description, not a STAR story — missing Situation and Result.
- Evidence (0/3): No numbers, timeline, or observable impact.
- Specificity (1/3): You named the model type and a high-level approach but no tools, company, or your role.

One concrete fix: Turn it into a 3–4 sentence STAR answer. Include:
- Situation: company/team and a specific problem (e.g., "monthly revenue fell X%").
- Task: your role/responsibility.
- Action: tools and steps (Excel, SQL, three-statement model, comps; how long it took).
- Result: a measurable outcome (reduced variance, dollars saved, decision made).
Tight rewrite you can copy and personalize:
"At [Company], our monthly forecast missed by 12% and leadership wanted a clearer outlook. As the financial analyst, I built a three‑statement model in [your skill] that started from product-level revenue drivers, added churn and pricing scenarios, and benchmarked assumptions to three public comps. I stress‑tested scenarios and produced a tightened forecast (variance narrowed from 10–30% to 5–8%) that supported a leadership decision to raise prices 4%, improving projected operating cash flow within one quarter."

Next question (when you're ready): do you want the tone formal (investor-facing) or collaborative (team-facing)?

Below is the exact, field-by-field list I will prepare on the application card for that posting when you give me the posting/link. I will fill each field only from confirmed facts on your account or what you type into the card; any missing item will appear as a bracketed prompt for you to fill before you approve submission. I assumed a typical employer careers form + optional ATS questions; tell me if this posting has something different and I will adapt.
What I'll prepare, field by field (exact content I'll put and where I'll ask you to confirm)

1) Posting reference
- What it is on the card: Employer name, job title, location, and the posting link or internal id as shown on the posting.
- What I'll fill: the exact title, company and location from the posting; the link; and the posting date if available.
2) Resume file (upload)
- What it is on the card: the PDF file the employer will receive.
- What I'll put: a tailored PDF built only from your confirmed facts. If you have not confirmed any facts yet, the card will show a draft resume and the top of the PDF will include [What name and email should go at top of resume?] and any other bracketed placeholders. You must approve the exact PDF before any submission.
3) Cover letter or short message
- What it is: either an uploaded cover letter or a short message the application form accepts (≤120 words for message forms).
- What I'll draft: a 1-paragraph tailored cover note that uses only confirmed facts; any missing details (team, specific metric, reason for interest) will be shown as [brackets]. If the posting has required open questions, I will draft concise answers to each with the same rule.
4) Contact info fields (name, email, phone, city/state)
- What it is: the form fields at the top of most applications.
- What I'll fill: exactly the name and email you type for the resume contact and the phone and city/state you confirm in the card. If you haven't given them in chat, the card will ask: "What name and email should go at the top of your resume?" and leave placeholders until you fill them.
5) Work authorization / eligibility questions
- What it is: yes/no or short answers about whether you are authorized to work where the job is (e.g., "Authorized to work in the US?").
- What I'll fill: exactly what you type into the card; I will not assume sponsorship or status. If you have a standing instruction about sponsorship, I will keep it.

6) Earliest start date / notice period
- What it is: a date or "immediately"/number of weeks.
- What I'll fill: whatever you enter in the card (or a bracketed placeholder if you leave it out).
7) Salary expectations / current compensation (if asked)
- What it is: a numeric field, range, or multiple-choice.
- What I'll fill: only numbers you provide in the card. If the posting lists pay, I will display that and—if you want—suggest an ask, but I will not submit any salary data without your explicit entry and approval.

8) Screening yes/no questions (e.g., years of experience, degree required, willingness to relocate, remote/on-site)
- What it is: required form screening questions.
- What I'll fill: answers based only on your confirmed facts. If you haven't confirmed the needed fact, the card will show a bracketed answer for you to complete.
9) Work history entries copied into form fields (employer, title, dates, duties) if the form asks
- What it is: parsed fields some forms require in addition to the resume upload.
- What I'll fill: I will map the entries from the tailored PDF I prepared. If any date, employer or title is missing or ambiguous, the card will show the exact bracketed text for you to fix.

10) Education fields (degree, school, graduation year)
- What it is: education details forms may request.
- What I'll fill: from your confirmed facts; otherwise bracketed prompts.
11) Attachments beyond resume/cover (portfolio, transcripts, certifications)
- What it is: additional files requested by the posting.
- What I'll do: attach only files you explicitly provided on file. If the posting asks for something you haven't uploaded, the card will show: [Attach X file] and will not attach anything until you do.

12) Optional profile fields (LinkedIn URL, GitHub, portfolio link, personal site)
- What it is: optional links the form may accept.
- What I'll fill: only links you put into the card; I will not guess or pull from elsewhere.
13) References
- What it is: names/emails or "Available upon request".
- What I'll fill: "Available upon request" by default unless you provide confirmed references in the card.

14) Voluntary self-ID / diversity fields
- What it is: optional demographic questions.
- What I'll do: leave blank unless you instruct otherwise in the card.

15) Final preview / summary line
- What it is: the final set of what will be submitted.
- What I'll show: one-line summary listing the resume filename, cover note text (or "none"), attachments, and the exact answers to required screening questions for your final approval.
16) Submission metadata I record (internal)

- What I'll record: the job id/link and the exact persona name used; this is only for tracking and will be shown on the card.
